_about: Each state's download, for .github/workflows/download.yml (and the restore steps in publish.yml, which check_site.py compares with this list). code: the data/<code> folder's name (nj covers nj and va); key: its cache's name; minutes: the download's time limit; run: the command.

states.name: New Jersey and Virginia
states.run: python3 states/nj/fetch.py; nj=$?; python3 states/va/fetch.py && exit $nj
states.note: v2: started fresh when the filled-in 2022-23 file went into git (states/nj/fill2022.py).

states.name: Texas
states.note: One file per bill; only changed files after the first copy.

states.name: Connecticut
states.note: A stuck FTP server once left a run with nothing: the last copy is kept.

states.name: Michigan
states.note: One request a second (the Legislature's limit).

states.name: Wisconsin
states.note: One request a second; the first copy takes several runs.

states.name: Arizona
states.run: python3 states/az/fetch.py; python3 states/az/azleg.py && python3 states/az/contacts.py
states.note: Open States (the free tier's daily quota), then azleg.gov at its two-minute crawl delay.

states.name: North Carolina
states.note: Two seconds apart (its robots.txt crawl delay).

states.name: Colorado
states.note: 3 seconds apart (it answers "too many requests" faster); members' votes fill in over many runs.

states.name: Utah
states.note: The developer API (UTAH_API_TOKEN), then members' votes from le.utah.gov at its 10-second crawl delay, 40 minutes a run.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.note: Roll calls at one request a second.

states.name: Indiana
states.run: python3 states/in/fetch.py && python3 states/in/contacts.py 2024 && python3 states/in/contacts.py 2025 && python3 states/in/contacts.py

states.name: Arkansas
states.run: python3 states/ar/fetch.py --votes && python3 states/ar/contacts.py 2023 && python3 states/ar/contacts.py 2024 && python3 states/ar/contacts.py 2025 && python3 states/ar/contacts.py

states.name: Alaska
states.run: python3 states/ak/fetch.py && python3 states/ak/contacts.py 2023 && python3 states/ak/contacts.py

states.name: LegiScan states
states.run: python3 legiscan.py tn ok me ri vt && python3 states/tn/contacts.py 2023 && python3 states/tn/contacts.py && python3 states/ok/contacts.py && python3 states/me/contacts.py && python3 states/ri/contacts.py && python3 states/vt/contacts.py
states.note: Tennessee, Oklahoma, Maine, Rhode Island and Vermont from LegiScan (LEGISCAN_API_KEY), in one job so they share one count of the month's queries (data/legiscan/usage.json; stops at 9,000 of the free 10,000).

states.name: New Hampshire
states.run: pip install -q pymssql pypdf && python3 states/nh/fetch.py && python3 states/nh/contacts.py
states.note: The General Court's daily data files (current year), plus its public read-only SQL Server for past years (login read each time from the Legislature's own document, never stored).

states.name: Minnesota
states.run: (command -v pdftotext >/dev/null || sudo apt-get install -y -qq poppler-utils >/dev/null) && python3 states/mn/fetch.py && python3 states/mn/contacts.py

states.name: Missouri
states.run: (command -v pdftotext >/dev/null || sudo apt-get install -y -qq poppler-utils >/dev/null) && python3 states/mo/fetch.py && python3 states/mo/contacts.py

states.name: West Virginia
states.run: (command -v pdftotext >/dev/null || sudo apt-get install -y -qq poppler-utils >/dev/null) && python3 states/wv/fetch.py && python3 states/wv/contacts.py

states.name: Nebraska
states.run: (command -v pdftotext >/dev/null || sudo apt-get install -y -qq poppler-utils >/dev/null) && python3 states/ne/fetch.py && python3 states/ne/contacts.py

states.name: New Mexico
states.run: (command -v pdftotext >/dev/null || sudo apt-get install -y -qq poppler-utils >/dev/null) && python3 states/nm/fetch.py && python3 states/nm/contacts.py

states.name: Hawaii
states.note: Open States (OPENSTATES_API_KEY), at most 110 requests a day so Arizona keeps the rest of the free tier's 250; the Legislature's own site blocks automated requests. Not built into the site until its converter exists.

states.name: Iowa
states.run: (command -v pdftotext >/dev/null || sudo apt-get install -y -qq poppler-utils >/dev/null) && python3 states/ia/fetch.py
states.note: legis.iowa.gov, a request every 6 seconds; a run ends at once if the site's bot check appears (the owner's choice, 2026-11-13). The first copy (about 28 hours of requests) builds up over many runs. Not built into the site until its converter exists.
